kind: Actual browser interactions with captions outside the app iframe; fictional sample notices

scenes.caption: Aftertext brings back teletext as a community bulletin you can edit, carry in a file and read offline.
Give a notice a page number. Type 201 to open the book swap. All notices in this example are fictional.
Reading view shows the full notice with ordinary text wrapping. It is also the default on a narrow phone.
Edit the current bulletin and watch its page preview. Each notice keeps its original words and spacing.
Long notices continue across subpages. The file preserves Unicode, newlines and spaces independently of the grid.
Turn the preview page to see the rest. Nothing is silently cut off to fit the screen.
Save the bulletin on this device. The reader and exported file now use the edited notice.
Export downloads the whole bulletin as a small JSON file. The byte count is measured from that file.
Open the exported file to restore the bulletin. The app does not upload it to a server.
Network disconnected, ordinary browser cache cleared, app reloaded. The saved bulletin still opens.
At phone width, reading view opens automatically. The same saved file stays available offline.
Built with Kiro CLI for the specification and initial validator, plus Codex for implementation and tests. Source and Kiro records accompany the demo.
